questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important that my study destination was located within Europe in order for my friends and family to easily come visit me. Further, the University had to provide courses in English, that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The website of UiB provides some good information to international students in terms of how to apply for exchange, student housing, insurance and so on. Therefore, it was easy to find the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at my student housing, the people working there helped me with some basic stuff and navigated me to my room. Further, the international center at UiB helped me with some technical difficulties.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find housing through the student welfare organization called Sammen. They even guarantee different housing options to new international students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most housing options off campus are located close to public transportation, which makes it easy to commute to the city center and UiB every day. For instance, it only takes 20 minutes with the tram from Fantoft.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UiB provides a list of courses available for international students from where you can choose from. After finding the courses that you want, you follow a guide on their website, which is not too complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to write the international center at UiB.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me, the registration process was very easy and without any complications.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the webpage "Courses for Exchange Students" at the website of UiB.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses are very similar to the ones at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was likewise very similar to that of UCPH, with some minor differences.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in Web Design I and Critical Approaches to Technology and Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses I was enrolled in are very relevant for the degree in Communication and IT, and I therefore recommend them to future exchange students that are interested in these topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on a lot of different trips around Norway, which I didn't plan before going to Bergen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most items are a bit more expensive than in Denmark. Alcohol is probably the most expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sammen offered different athletic activities, such as a gym membership (including swimming pool), golf simulator and indoor climbing. The student house called "Det Akademiske Kvarter" offered different social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It is almost a must to hike the mountains of Bergen! It is also worth going on trips around Norway and experience the Norwegian nature (maybe even the Northern Lights). I also recommend to hang out with your friends or make new ones, drink some coffees, play games and go partying.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, as their culture is similar to the Danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The easiest way to meet and socialize with local students is through the courses you take and through social activities throughout Bergen. A lot of local students go to Det Akademiske Kvarter, and it is therefore a great place to socialize with them. It might also be worth volunteering there!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked that it was somewhat similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. A lot of people warned me about the rain in Bergen before going. However, the rain was not bad at all - it rained just as much as it rained in Denmark. So don't be terrified if people warn you about it.

2. Make an effort to meet new people. It will make your stay so much better!

3. Go explore the Norwegian nature!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have to be 20+ to enter most bars and clubs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many new people and make friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was to share a room and not really having a private space. However, it became easier as my roommate and I got to know each other!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
